_note: Static instruction fragments for Decision-1, filled in by stage 1's rules (decision_router/instructions.py). A fragment is used when every condition in `when` holds and every placeholder has a value; used fragments are joined in this order. `when` keys: mode, profile, action (any listed action is requested), band (named | range | group), has (all listed facts are true). If the text is longer than max_chars, fragments are dropped from the end, never base or mode. A request with no extras renders exactly the catalog's routing-mode instructions. See docs/DECISION1_INSTRUCTIONS.md.

fragments.text: Choose the model that should answer the conversation in the state.
Cost mode: choose the cheapest model that can still answer well. Prefer a more expensive model only when a cheaper one would likely give a wrong or incomplete answer.
Balanced mode: weigh answer quality against cost. Prefer a cheaper model when its answer would be about as good as the best model's answer.
Quality mode: choose the model most likely to give the best answer. Ignore cost.
The caller is a coding agent that works over many turns: prefer a model that is reliable at multi-step tool use and keeps a consistent approach across turns.
The task is software engineering: prefer a model that finds the root cause before changing code and checks its own work.
The task is to evaluate or review: prefer a model that judges carefully against the stated criteria and explains its verdict.
The task is extraction: prefer a model that copies values exactly and leaves out what is not in the source.
The task is to orchestrate steps or agents: prefer a model that follows the plan and calls tools in the right order.
The task is planning: prefer a model that breaks the goal into concrete, ordered steps and notes the risks.
The task needs multi-step reasoning: prefer a model that works through the problem rather than answering from pattern.
The task is summarisation: prefer a model that keeps the key facts and adds nothing that is not in the source.
The task is translation: prefer a model that keeps the meaning, tone and terminology of the source.
The task is writing: prefer a model whose text needs little editing and makes no unsupported claims.
The caller asked for the {band_label} cost band: the {candidate_count} options cost ${price_min} to ${price_max} per million output tokens.
The caller asked for output prices of {band_label} per million tokens: the {candidate_count} options cost ${price_min} to ${price_max}.
The options are the {band_label} price group of the models suited to {actions}: {candidate_count} options costing ${price_min} to ${price_max} per million output tokens.
The request offers tools ({tool_names}) and every option can call them: prefer the option most reliable at choosing and sequencing tool calls.
The answer must follow a JSON schema and every option supports this: judge on the content.
The request includes {image_count} image(s): prefer the option with the strongest image understanding.
The caller asked for a model with a reasoning mode; every option has one.
The prompt is about {prompt_tokens} tokens: prefer an option that stays accurate over long inputs.
The answer may run to {output_tokens} tokens: prefer an option that stays coherent over long outputs.
This conversation was answered by {previous_model}, which can no longer serve it ({pin_reason}): prefer an option that can continue that work with the least disruption.
The request is a native Anthropic Messages body and every option is a Claude model.

criteria.priced: {description} Price per million tokens: ${input_price} input, ${output_price} output; {price_rank} of {candidate_count} by price among these options, ordered by output price then input price (1 is cheapest).
criteria.unpriced: {description} {price_rank} of {candidate_count} by price among these options (1 is cheapest).
